title: Sajeel Ahmed- VS -FOP etc.
text:
Form No: HCJD/C-121 
ORDER SHEET. 
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD. 
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT. 
 
 
 
Writ Petition. No.4567 of 2025 
 
Sajeel Ahmad 
VS 
Federation of Pakistan through M/o Interior and others 
S. No. of order/ 
proceedings 
Date of  order/ 
Proceedings 
Order with signature of Judge and that of parties or 
counsel where necessary.  
 
05.01.2026
Mr. Zeeshan Gohar, Advocate for the petitioner. 
Ms. Shaista Tabassum, learned AAG.  
Imtiaz Hussain Hashmi, Assistant Law Officer, DG 
IMPASS.  
 
 
  
The petitioner, through this petition, assails the placement of 
his name on the Passport Control List (“PCL”).  
 
2. 
It was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for the 
petitioner that the act of placing/retaining the petitioner’s name on 
the PCL is arbitrary, without lawful authority, and violates the 
petitioner's fundamental rights under Articles 4, 9, 10-A, 15, and 18 
of the Constitution. He, thus, prays for acceptance of this petition. 
 
3. 
The respondents, in their detailed report, have submitted that 
the petitioner's name was placed on the PCL 08.10.2024. This action 
was based on a report from the Consulate General of Pakistan, Dubai 
(UAE), indicating that the petitioner was deported from the UAE after 
being jailed. The respondents assert that this action was taken in 
accordance with Rules 21 and 22 of the Passport Rules, 2021. 
Importantly, the respondents have pointed out the existence of a 
statutory alternate remedy. They have drawn the Court's attention to 
Rule 22(2)(c) & (3)(b) of the Passport Rules, 2021, which establishes 
a Review Committee. This Committee, chaired by the Director 
General of Immigration & Passports, is specifically empowered to 
consider appeals for the omission of a name from the PCL before the 
normal stipulated period of five years. 
 
4. 
Heard. Record perused.  
 
5. 
A cardinal and well-settled principle of constitutional 
jurisprudence is that a High Court, in the exercise of its discretionary 
jurisdiction under Article 199 of the Constitution, will not ordinarily 
intervene where an equally efficacious, alternative, and adequate 
statutory remedy is available to the aggrieved party. The underlying

rationale for this doctrine is to prevent litigants from circumventing 
established 
statutory 
frameworks 
and 
to 
ensure 
that 
the 
extraordinary writ jurisdiction is not diluted into a court of first 
appeal. This principle finds steadfast support in the judgment of the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. Sher Afgan Niazi v. All S. Habib (2011 
SCMR 1813). 
 
6. 
In the present case, the statutory framework of the Passport 
Rules, 2021, provides a complete mechanism not only for placement 
on the PCL but also for review and removal. The petitioner has the 
statutory right to file an appeal/review application before the 
competent Review Committee, which is the designated forum to 
examine the factual matrix of each case, including the grounds for 
deportation, the nature of the offence, and any subsequent 
developments or representations. 
 
7. 
Consequently, without expressing any opinion on the merits 
of the petitioner's claims or the respondents' defences, this petition is 
disposed of with the direction to the petitioner to file a 
comprehensive application/appeal before the Review Committee 
constituted under Rule 22 of the Passport Rules, 2021, within a 
period of one week from today. If such an application is filed, the 
Review Committee is directed to decide the same on its own merits, 
in accordance with the law, after affording the petitioner an 
opportunity of hearing, within a period of seven (07) days from the 
date of its filing.  
 
 
 
          (MUHAMMAD ASIF)      
                     JUDGE                         
 
 
Ahmed Sheikh
